newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says dlr better matches fundamentals - paper.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says dlr better matches fundamentals - paper.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel said on Friday the current dollar rate better matched economic fundamentals and helped strengthen German exports.

Asked in an interview with the Berlin daily B.Z. whether the recent slide in the mark was an advantage for the German economy, Waigel said, "There can be no question of losses. The current development is much more of a normalisation.

"The mark was overvalued against other important currencies in 1995 and 1996. Now we are around the average level of the years 1990 and 1994. This is a situation which better matches the economic fundamentals. It also strengthens our exports," he added.
Waigel will join other leaders of the Group of Seven industrial nations in Berlin on Saturday to discuss the state of world growth, with the recent rapid rise in the dollar high on the agenda.

Waigel told the newspaper that cooperation within the G7 -- which alongside Germany includes Britain, Canada, France, Italy, Japan and the United States -- was a central prerequisite for stable economic conditions.

He added that structural problems in Europe, seen as main cause of high unemployment there, would also be addressed in Saturday's G7 talks. In Germany, tax cuts from a planned overhaul of the system would play a key role, he said.
Waigel admitted that German growth had fallen behind that of other G7 countries, but added that the economy could nonetheless not be described as weak.
"We have to make more effort to adjust to global change and to bring it about ourselves," he said.
Waigel said there were no current plans to extend the G7 to include upcoming industrial nations such as South Korea.

But he added, "Of course it is desirable if more countries are prepared to take over responsibility for a stable international trading and currency system and also to offer financial help for this. But this does not have to be as a member of the G7," he said.
